newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER STEADY AT NOON, UNMOVED BY RINGGIT.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER STEADY AT NOON, UNMOVED BY RINGGIT.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market was unchanged on Monday noon, with government officials saying there was no demand to warrant price adjustments.
But traders argued that higher prices quotes were necessary to at least reflect the continuous weakening of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar.
"There's hardly anything happening, of course, but I still think that the price must be a little higher because of the strong dollar," said a trader.
"We are trading in ringgit but Indonesia is doing in it dollars, and they have already made the adjustment," added the trader.
The ringgit fell to fresh 42-month lows against the dollar in late morning trading on Monday on continued sales by offshore and local players, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7210/40 to a dollar, its lowest level since March 28, 1994.
At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for September buyer at 247.50 cents (91 U.S. cents) a kg, unchanged from Friday's close.
The SMR20 for September buyer was also unchanged at 246.00 cents a kg.
